- **RUL77 (posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". 1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `/account-locks///`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp--`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env.

Residual: a writing unit after an integrate step still starts from the main checkout's HEAD, not the integrate target. - **RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed; dispatch is the lower layer and fanout belongs to the Work layer, 2026-10-14; decision 0062, replaces the purpose-door part of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch) and the one-posture-lane-per-door part of RUL77 (posture belongs to the capability)).** Work is executed through two doors only, `fgos run` (`""`, `--unit`, `--resume`) and `fgos workflow start`, both on `runUnit`. `dispatch execute` (executor id, `--contract`, `--assignment`), `dispatch log` and `dispatch fanout-batch` are gone, with `src/runner/dispatch-log.mjs`; calling `dispatch execute` (any form) or `dispatch log` returns a `validation` error with one sentence naming the replacement (`fgos run "" [--provider ] [--capability ] [--writes …]` or `fgos run --unit`, where `--provider` is named only for an agent executor — `fgos run` refuses any other kind — the `--for` capability is kept when it is registered, and a tool executor's caller is told to call that tool directly; the dispatch-decide hook's BLOCKED message is built the same way, by `runDoorHint`; `fgos run --unit` or a Workflow for `--assignment`; provenance under `.fgos/assignments//` for `dispatch log`), from one place in `bin`, also for `returnResult` callers. `executeExecutorCli` has no CLI door left: it is the transport step of an Assignment (`assignment-runner.mjs`), and its one other caller, `fanout-batch.mjs`, is listed in `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` until fanout runs on `runUnit`; `fgos dispatch` keeps `decide`, `inspect`, `reconcile` and `probe-account`. `src/runner/dispatch.mjs` imports nothing from the Work layer: `decide --work` gets its Work resolver injected from `bin`, so it runs only as `fgos dispatch decide --work`. A Unit's posture comes from its `writes` (none: read-only, sandboxed; some: mutating, in a linked worktree) plus the capability's required confinement, never from which door was used. Fanout adds no verb: `node src/runner/fanout-batch.mjs "" [--has-live-task-access]` prints `fired`, `mechanismChanged`, `unavailable`, `deferred` (plus `slotsFull: true` when no slot was free); its body moves onto `runUnit` with the Work-layer cut. An import guard (`test/architecture.test.mjs`) keeps `dispatch.mjs` and `src/workflow/**` free of Work imports, following relative imports transitively (a re-export one or more hops away counts) and reading `require()` and literal `import()`; a call-site guard over `src`, `bin`, `scripts`, `domains` and `core` names the files allowed to call `executeAssignment`, `executeExecutorCli`, `commitUnitWork` and `executeThroughConfinement` (an aliased, destructured or namespace use counts as a call; `export *` from their home modules is refused), with Work-layer callers not yet on `runUnit` listed in `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS`, compared by equality so the list can only shrink. An `import()` with a non-literal specifier is not yet seen by the import guard (left to the dispatch-generic-inputs phase). [Closed by RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only): a computed `import()`/`require()`, `createRequire`, `node:module` and `eval` are refused in the guarded files outside a named allowlist; `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` is empty and deleted.] The doctrine test `test/docs/run-doors-doctrine.test.mjs` refuses `AGENTS.md`, any skill source or any render that still teaches a removed door. - **RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run; the pin is hard and never bypasses the lease, 2026-10-14).** `fgos run --account `, or an `account` key on an `--override` object (one shape; a Unit carries no account), pins a provider account (`src/runner/execution/account-pin.mjs`). `bind()` pins it on each seat its override reaches whose bound executor's provider (normalized as the lease does) lists it in `providers..accounts`: `binding.account = { provider, id }`, `provenance.account = { value, source: override: }`. A seat on another provider (a checker must use another family), an executor without an account list, and a tool or inline binding bind unpinned with `provenance.account.skipped { reason, detail }`; the pin never chooses the executor (pair it with `--provider`); a malformed id is refused (`account-pin-invalid`), and an inherited object key is never an account id. Before the unit run exists the seats are dry-bound as the run would bind them (`simulateUnitBindings` with the run's overrides): a pin no seat takes, or a quarantined account (the message names `until` and the reason code), is refused. A pinned seat is dispatched with the inventory narrowed to its account (`configPinnedToAccount`, as RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI) does), so the lease, quarantine and governance apply unchanged. A provider limit on a pinned seat ends it (`fallbackExhausted.reason: account-pinned`, `retryStopped` on the attempt): no account rotation, no executor failover. `--account` is refused with `--resume`; a resumed run keeps its bindings' account and is refused while that account is quarantined. Left open: the login store per CLI (RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI)) is checked only by the lease at dispatch, after the unit run exists; `capacityProviderOf` derives the provider from the executor entry and can differ from the lease's for an executor that declares no `providerModel` (every configured executor declares one); `fgos workflow start` has no `--account`. - **RUL92 (a writing seat is not run again over its own partial writes after a provider limit, 2026-10-14).** At every launch of a seat that writes (a resumed launch included), the runner records the worktree's HEAD and the content of every path `git status` sees as changed (`writeBaseline` on the attempt, `src/runner/execution/partial-writes.mjs`; `.fgos/` left out, a symlink by its target, an unreadable file by size and mtime). When the seat stops on a provider limit and the worktree differs (a write, rename, delete, a further change to a file already dirty, a moved HEAD), it is not rotated to another account nor walked to another candidate: the seat ends `provider-limit` with `fallbackExhausted: { reason: partial-writes, paths, headMoved }` and `retryStopped` on the attempt, for a person to keep, finish or undo the changes and resume. This check runs before the pinned stop of RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run), so a pinned seat still names what it changed (`accountPinned`). A read-only seat records no baseline and rotates as before (its sandbox keeps the worktree; a concurrent `verify` write never stops it), as does a writing seat that left the worktree as it was; a baseline git could not take stops the retry. Not seen: gitignored paths, `.fgos/` inside the worktree, changes inside a nested repository or a dirty submodule, a mode-only change to a file already dirty; none of them reaches the runner's commit, which takes only the write scope. - **RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each, 2026-10-14; ends the `spawnWorker` purpose door of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch) and the `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` entries of RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed) for `loop.mjs`, `work-dispatch.mjs` and `fanout-batch.mjs`).** `spawnWorker` (`src/runner/work-dispatch.mjs`) builds the item's Unit with `workUnitFor` and runs it through `runUnit` in the item's worktree, with `session { headless: true, herdrPresent: false }` (the loop never opens a pane, even when the runner itself runs inside herdr); `fanout-batch.mjs` does the same per candidate after `pick`, then `fgos return` on `pass` (no `--worker-verified-sha`: return judges the Unit run's commit) or `return --to blocked` otherwise, reporting each `fired` entry as `{id, unitRunId, outcome, commit}`. The worker runs confined and never commits; the Unit run commits a passing round inside its `writes` (`['**']` for a step), and the loop reads `commit` (`runner`, `none`, or `self` when HEAD moved without a runner commit) instead of committing itself. A step Unit names its capability as its domain's Workflow units do, `:` (`coding:discover`), except the coding executing step, which keeps `code:implement`; `bind()` falls back to the bare verb, and `fgos doctor`'s `workflow-capabilities-configured` also names `code:implement` (`RUNNER_LOOP_CAPABILITY_USES`). The worker config is the repo's `.fgos/config.json` (snapshotted into `unit.json`): `fgos-runner` has no `--config` any more. Outcomes map onto the recovery matrix (`src/runner/recovery.mjs`): a failed runner commit, or an index staged before launch, is `worktree-fail`; a timeout `worker-timeout`; a command that cannot start `worker-spawn-fail`; every candidate at its provider limit `provider-limit` (park); a refusal before any worker started `no-executor` (park, the message names `runner.capabilities[""].prefer`), so one capability without a runnable pool never halts the runner; a round that ran, did not pass and left uncommitted files `worker-failed` (retry), so goal-check never judges files that are not on the branch; a round that did not pass and left nothing resolves with `commit: none` and goal-check decides on the branch as it stands. A round that stopped over its own partial writes (RUL92 (a writing seat is not run again over its own partial writes after a provider limit)) or whose runner commit failed keeps its worktree: the loop notes `{unitRunId, worktree}` under `.fgos/runtime/runner-resume/.json`, and the item's next attempt (a retry, or a later dispatch once the item is back at `todo`) resumes that same Unit run there, so a failed commit is committed again without spawning the agent; the note is checked against `unit.json` (same Unit id, worktree still checked out on `fgw/`) and dropped once the run no longer needs it. The Unit's rigor comes from the operation, then the item's `rigor`, with `risk: heavy` read as `high` only when no `rigor` is declared; bind's floor raises `low` to `standard`. The item's `refs` and `docsRef` enter the Unit only as safe repo-relative paths (others are dropped with a warning that reaches the loop log), and its `prefer` names the step's executor only when that executor is registered. The executor dispatch event carries `unitRunId`; the item log names the run the moment it exists and where its output is captured (`protected/capture/` while it runs, `stdout.log` once it settles), since a Unit run streams nothing back; a write into the main checkout during the round reaches the loop log as a `stray-write-correlated` warning. A pane run's `stdout.log` holds the settled report's text, so a worker run in a pane must put its `fgos-verdict`/`fgos-discovered` fences in its report; the loop reads the first non-empty of report, `stdout.log` and claim summary, never several. The startup reap keeps a 0-commit `fgw/` branch that a killed round still has checked out, with its uncommitted work, instead of failing on the branch delete. Not done: the loop does not resume a Unit run left `running` by a killed runner (the run id is in the item log; `fgos run --resume `); a worker detached from a killed runner may outlive it; a commit subject falls back to `producer changes` when the worker wrote no claim. - **RUL94 (a Work driver step runs as a Unit: the step's declared operation, pinned inputs, and a verdict bound to their bytes, 2026-10-14; ends the `operation-choice.mjs` entry of `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` from RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed)).** A driver step of a work item (`fgos plan --validate`, the runner loop's validate-plan and secondary operations) is built by `workUnitFor` and run through `runUnit`, never by `executeAssignment` (`src/runner/operation-choice.mjs`). `runUnit` takes `declared: {workId, domain, workflow, stage, operation, operations}` (the step's operation objects), `pinInputs` (absolute paths) and `runnerConfig` (the config the caller resolved, snapshotted instead of `.fgos/config.json`, so one step reads one config); `declared` and `pinInputs` are kept in `unit.json` and a resume reads them, and the pattern, from there. Refused before the unit directory exists: an operation the step does not declare, a `human-only` one, a stamped mutation that disagrees with the unit's `writes` (read-only exactly when it writes nothing), and any pattern that does not resolve to `solo`. Only the producer seat carries the operation: its assignment has the operation's role and normalizer stamp (`mutation`, `evidence`, `resultKind`, `onAdvance`, built by `declaredOperationFields` in `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs`, shared with `buildAssignment`), the seat name stays in `provenance.role`, and `policy.rigor` is the unit's rigor. At launch the dispatch hashes each pin into `inputDigests[{path, root, rel, sha256}]` in `run.json` and `result.json`; a pin is read only when its real path lies in the main checkout or a worktree git lists (not one that became a symlink), against the innermost such root, else its `sha256` is `null` and nothing is read. The verdict walker (`findLatestAssignmentRunResult`) reads flat and nested layouts through `listAssignmentRuns`, filters by `operation`, takes only a unit run's producer seat, and compares the current `plan.md` by `rel` and digest; a pinned digest decides alone (no mtime pre-filter), so a plan merged byte for byte into another checkout still matches, and `planContentHash` is only read on results from before this rule. The driver hands the producer's own RunResult and seat assignment to `interpretAssignmentRunResult`, stops on a unit with no result or whose runner commit failed (`unit-commit-failed`), and never turns an item ref naming another run's output (`unit-run:`, `gate-answer:`) into an input. The worker is confined (`session: {headless: true, herdrPresent: false}`): a read-only operation cannot write the checkout, and a machine with no confinement backend stops the step (`unit-refused-posture-unavailable`). A unit with `rigor: low` is raised to `standard` by bind's floor. Not done here: a pin resolved through `process.cwd()` first (`resolveContentRoot`) can differ from the plan in the item worktree a secondary operation runs in. - **RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only; Work is a consumer, 2026-10-14; decision 0063, replaces the input part of RUL73 (dispatch does not know Work).2 and closes the `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` list of RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed)).** `src/runner/dispatch/**`, `src/runner/execution/**`, `src/runner/dispatch.mjs` and `src/workflow/**` never handle a Work item. Rigor and domain are the assignment's own fields: `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` reads `assignment.rigor` where it read `work.rigor`/`work.risk` (first explicit source may pick it, after an operation rigor it only raises, the capability floor and tier rules are unchanged; provenance scope `assignment`) and `assignment.domain` for the `:review` capability floor, so a declared Unit step (whose seat carries `domain`) gets that floor again. The Work layer folds an item's `rigor` and `risk: heavy` into one rigor (`workRigorFor`). `decide --work` gets a hint from the Work layer, `workDispatchHint`/`resolveWorkForDispatch` → `{workExecutorId, agentType, rigor?, domain?}`, passed to `compileDispatchPlan({workId, workHint})`; fan-out uses the same hint. `workDispatchContext` returns only `{capabilityHints, agentType}`. `buildAssignment`, `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`, `compileDispatchPlan`, `decideExecutorCli`, `executeExecutorCli` and `executeAssignment` refuse a `work`, `workItem` or `workExecutorId` input (`RunnerConfigError` "takes no Work item") instead of ignoring it; `decideExecutorCli` and `compileDispatchPlan` name the `--work` selector `workId`. `executeExecutorCli` no longer runs an unregistered executor id because a Work item rode along (`executor-not-found`). A domain's contract harness (ADR-007) is loaded only by the Work layer (`domainHarnessFor(work, {domain})`, only for a registered domain at a declared step; `loadHarnessModule` treats a module that fails to import as no harness), and a caller hands it to the inline `buildAssignment` as `options.domainHarness`; dispatch still re-validates the enriched contract and records `domain-harness-seam`. No production path builds an inline assignment for a Work item today (none did before either: the only inline caller is `probe-account`), so the seam runs only in tests. The guard (`test/architecture.test.mjs`) refuses, outside comments and other string text, any identifier or property named `work`, `workItem` or `docsRef` (identifier escapes such as `\u0077ork` are decoded first), any string that is exactly one of those names (a computed or quoted key, `Reflect.get(o, 'work')`, a key comparison; only the pinned uses are allowed: the `--work` selector's type in `plan.mjs` and the refused option names in `assignment-policy.mjs`), and any `resolveContentRoot(` call in the guarded files; `src/state/**` counts as Work layer for the transitive import guard, except one pinned edge (`worktree.mjs` takes only `StoreError` from `src/state/store.mjs`); imports are read with optional whitespace, comments blanked, `?query` dropped, and absolute paths and `file:` URLs resolved; the guarded folders may hold only plain `.mjs` files (no `.js`/`.cjs`/TypeScript source, no symlink); the shared source lexer treats a slash after a block's closing brace as a regular expression, so its quotes cannot hide the code after it; it also refuses an `import()`/`require()` whose specifier is not one plain literal, `createRequire`, `eval`, `Function(...)` (with or without `new`) and an import of `module`, `vm` or `worker_threads` (with or without `node:`), except the loads pinned one by one in a named allowlist entry with its reason (`provider-credential-renewal.mjs`: `createRequire` for `node:sqlite`); one more load in an allowlisted file fails too. The call-site guard also counts a string that is exactly a door's name (`d['executeAssignment'](a)`) and an escaped name as a use, and compares each run door with exactly its named callers (`executeAssignment`: `execution/run.mjs`, `dispatch/cli.mjs`; `executeExecutorCli`: `dispatch/assignment-runner.mjs`; `commitUnitWork`: `execution/run.mjs`; `executeThroughConfinement`: `dispatch/cli.mjs`), both ways. Not covered: a name built at run time (`opts[k]`, `opts['wo' + 'rk']`, `globalThis['ev' + 'al']`), nested inputs (`options.work`, `assignment.work`; nothing reads them), and code outside the guarded files that reaches into dispatch's internals. - **RUL96 (one run may take its own timeout, from 1m to 4h; its private home and worktree lock last as long, 2026-10-15).** A unit run's seats are dispatched with `runner.timeoutMs` unless the run asks for its own: `fgos run --timeout ` (a whole number and one unit, `ms|s|m|h`: `90m`, `5400s`), a `timeoutMs` key on an `--override` object (`--timeout` adds it to every override that names none, and an unscoped one when none is unscoped, as `--effort` does), or a Unit's `timeoutMs` (whole milliseconds; a units file and a Workflow unit template carry it too, a template's value is checked when the definition loads). `bind()` resolves override, then unit, into `binding.timeoutMs` with `provenance.timeoutMs { value, source: override: | unit | none }`; a value outside the range is a refused binding (`run-timeout`), and an override's value is checked before the unit run exists. The value lives in `unit.json` (`overrides`, `unit`, and every recorded binding), so a resume dispatches with it and `--timeout` is refused with `--resume`; `runUnit` hands it to `executeAssignment` (`opts.timeoutMs ?? cfg.timeoutMs`), which already threads it to the worker kill, the pane poll and the dispatch lock. Range (`src/runner/dispatch/run-timeout.mjs`): the 1m floor keeps a typo (`90s` for `90m`) from killing a turn at once; the 4h ceiling, four times the heaviest turn seen, bounds how long a hung worker holds its worktree's lock and a copy of an account login, and `runner.timeoutMs` above it is refused when the config loads, so the default obeys it too. The confinement reaper keeps a home whose dispatcher pid is alive and has no pane until `createdAt + max(maxAgeMs, min(marker.timeoutMs, 4h) + 10m)` (the bwrap driver records the dispatch's `timeoutMs` in the ownership marker; a marker without one keeps the 1h rule; a dead dispatcher's home goes at once, a pane-retained home is unchanged), so a pane-less run longer than an hour is no longer reaped mid-turn. The per-worktree dispatch lock (`.fgos/dispatch--.lock`, composite `pid:acquiredAtMs:rand` holder) records the `ttlMs` its holder took and keeps it across renewals; a contender judges a live composite holder by the longer of its own ttl and the holder's, so a dispatch with a shorter timeout never takes the lock of a longer run that renews only every third of its own timeout; the recorded ttl is honoured only up to the 4h ceiling. Other lock identities are judged as before. Residual: a holder killed without releasing whose pid was reused reads as live (no process start time is recorded), so it now blocks the worktree for up to its own ttl (at most 4h) instead of the contender's; `fgos dispatch reconcile` clears such a lock by hand. `--override` passed with `--resume` is ignored, as for every override key (the run keeps `unit.json#overrides`). - **RUL97 (a Unit may sync a base ref first: the runner merges it, the worker only edits the conflicted files, 2026-10-15).** A Unit may carry `syncBase` (a branch, tag or commit name: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/`, `-`, not starting with `-` or `/`, no `..`); it needs `writes` and a linked worktree, and `fgos run --sync ` sets it (with a prompt: sync, then the task; without one: a sync-only Unit, `syncOnly: true`, whose objective is `Merge into this branch.`). The ref is resolved to a commit once, before the unit run exists (a ref naming no commit, or a run from the main checkout, leaves nothing behind), and `unit.json#sync` keeps `{ ref, sha, status, head?, conflicts?, mergeStaged?, commit? }`; a resume merges that sha, never the ref again. Before any seat runs, the runner merges it with the trusted git of RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope) — `merge --no-commit --no-ff`, rerere and autostash off — in `src/runner/execution/commit-unit-work.mjs` (`startSyncMerge`, `finishSyncMerge`, `syncMergeState`), orchestrated by `src/runner/execution/unit-sync.mjs`: already in the branch is `up-to-date`; a clean merge is committed by the runner as `chore(sync): merge ` (status `merged`; a commit that is not the merge of `sha` over `head` holding exactly what the merge staged — a hook added a file — fails `committed-set-mismatch` as `execution-failure`, stays on the branch, and the resume is refused until a person takes it off) and the Unit goes on to its pattern, or passes at once when sync-only; a sync never brings the base side of `.fgos/` in: every `.fgos/**` path the merge staged or left conflicted, clean or not, is put back to the branch side (HEAD), a path the base deleted is kept and a path only the base has is not taken — ADR0020 (a worker branch never commits `.fgos/`), the side `fgos-write-rejected` at approve resolves to the target for a `.fgos/` path the branch left unchanged, on every branch, not only `fgw/*`; any other conflict leaves the merge open (status `conflicted`), puts the conflicted paths the scope does not already cover in scope only while the merge is open (`sync.scopeAdded`, read by the effective scope only while `sync.status === 'conflicted'`; `writeScope` itself stays as declared, so a later round cannot write them), and appends a `## Merge to finish` section to the writing seat's brief naming them and telling it never to run git. A refused start leaves no merge open and ends the run: `merge-in-progress` (a merge someone else opened), `foreign-staged-index`, `merge-refused` (git would not start, e.g. a dirty file it would overwrite), `hook-refused` (the pre-commit hook of the main checkout's hooks path refused the clean merge commit; told apart from a git failure by running that hook once more as git runs it, and its words are the detail), `unscopable-conflict-path` (a conflicted path the scope normalizer of RUL84 (one write-scope matcher) would read differently — `*`, a leading `:`, `\`, surrounding whitespace — or holding a control character, since it is also printed into the brief; the merge is aborted) as `policy-refusal`, and `git-error` as `execution-failure`. While the merge is open, the preflight of a writing seat counts only the open MERGE_HEAD equal to `sync.sha` over `sync.head` as the run's own: its conflicted and merge-staged paths are neither a foreign index nor `preExistingInScope`; any other open merge refuses a writing seat (`merge-in-progress`) and `commitUnitWork` never commits over one. After a passing round the runner concludes the merge before the round's own commit: a conflicted file that still holds a line opening with seven or more `<`, `|` or `>` (a larger `conflict-marker-size` included; a file holding a NUL byte is read as binary and not checked) fails the commit `conflict-markers` with `paths`, stages nothing and keeps the merge, so `fgos run --resume` only commits once a person removed them (RUL86 (`fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits)); otherwise it stages the conflicted paths, refuses an index holding anything the merge did not stage (`staged-set-mismatch`, taking back what it staged itself, e.g. a conflicted file the worker turned into a directory), commits with MERGE_HEAD as second parent (a refusing pre-commit hook fails it `hook-refused` with the hook's words and keeps the merge; each `fgos run --resume` tries the commit once, never in a loop), checks parents and committed set (`committed-set-mismatch`), and then commits the rest of the round inside the scope as usual. The round's `commit` carries the merge's own record under `sync`; `runUnit` returns `sync` beside `outcome`; a sync-only unit that needed no worker returns one result `{ role: 'sync', round: 0, commit }` (no `verify`, as for `solo`). A round that did not pass keeps the merge open; a resume checks it first: still open, it runs the seat again over it; concluded by hand (its sha in the branch), it is `merged`; aborted, or HEAD moved, the resume is refused and names the merge. A run that died between starting git and recording the result adopts its own open merge on resume; a first start never adopts one. A resumed sync-only run that was `up-to-date` or `merged` passes again without a worker. Settlement: the writing seat over an open merge carries `assignment.syncConflicts`; those files, dirty at launch, changed during the turn and inside its scope, count as its evidence (`evidence.editedSyncConflicts`), so a seat that only resolves conflicts is not scored `verdict-inconclusive`. Any other file dirty at launch that a seat rewrites still is no evidence, with or without a sync. A units file (`fgos workflow start --units`) naming `syncBase` is refused: a workflow unit's worktree starts from its dependency's branch, and a sync there is not built. Not done: an inline producer over an open merge (inline rounds have no runner commit), a modify/delete conflict whose worker deletes the file is concluded as a deletion.

unit.sample: - **RUL1 (sự thật duy nhất là nhật ký sự kiện append-only, bản chiếu chỉ là dẫn xuất).** Trong vòng dispatch, runner là người ghi duy nhất qua một cửa; worker không bao giờ tự ghi
unit.text:
- **RUL1 (sự thật duy nhất là nhật ký sự kiện append-only, bản chiếu chỉ là dẫn xuất).** Trong vòng dispatch, runner là người ghi duy nhất qua một cửa; worker không bao giờ tự ghi trạng thái (per phase-2-routing / feed7428).
- **RUL2 (mọi mutation đi qua đúng một cửa ghi).** Kết quả worker là ĐỀ XUẤT mức bền: commit trên nhánh `fgw/` (do runner tạo từ file worker để lại, không phải worker tự commit — 0052), phải qua người duyệt mới thành `done`; không bao giờ tự merge (auto-merge là backlog STR9).
- **RUL3 (thứ tự ghi bất biến: sự kiện vào nhật ký trước, bản chiếu cập nhật sau).** Runner tự chạy proof của việc làm goal-check — lời trợ lý không bao giờ là bằng chứng.
- **RUL4 (giao việc theo mẻ, giới hạn hai tầng, quyền-sở-hữu-gốc giữ nguyên trong lượt chạy).** Một lượt chạy giao TỐI ĐA N việc cùng lúc, giới hạn qua cấu hình hai tầng — số gốc đồng thời × số con đồng thời mỗi gốc (Data Dictionary #6); mọi con của MỘT gốc luôn về tay cùng một chủ trong suốt một lượt chạy (Data Dictionary #7, xem RUL26 (quyền-sở-hữu-gốc — mọi con của một gốc về tay cùng một chủ trong một lượt chạy)); dispatch nạp lại mẻ tới khi không còn việc đang chạy VÀ không còn việc sẵn-sàng. Chống-lặp qua vận hành thật (A1) là điều kiện đã chứng minh TRƯỚC khi song song được dựng — không còn là một ngưỡng-tên treo chờ (per fan-out-parallel / 2e92b7a5).
- **RUL5 (ghi có kỳ vọng: trạng thái thực khác kỳ vọng thì từ chối, không ghi đè mù).** Model chọn theo tier của việc qua bảng cấu hình; tập tier reconcile một nguồn tại đây.
- **RUL6 (consumer rẽ nhánh theo mã thoát phạm trù, không bao giờ theo thông điệp).** Chống đỡ bằng CHỈ DẪN + nhánh-vứt-được, KHÔNG phải sandbox OS/container. Worker headless chạy dưới tập quyền TỐI THIỂU khai tường minh trong `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner.executor.args`: `--permission-mode acceptEdits` (tự nhận sửa file), **không** cấp quyền git — worker chỉ sửa file, runner commit thay (quyết định 0052; trước đó là `--allowedTools "Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)"`); `--dangerously-skip-permissions` bị BÁC có chủ đích (worker chỉ cần sửa-file + commit trong worktree, prompt đã cấm merge/push/tự gọi fgos, và goal-check không tin lời trợ lý — RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại) — nên quyền rộng hơn là rủi ro không cần) (per worker-execution / 22699c61, 04a6cd05). Root cause spike-proven (2 biến thể, claude CLI thật): thiếu allowlist này, headless `claude -p` sửa file được nhưng `git commit` treo vô thời hạn chờ duyệt tương tác → nhánh đề xuất luôn rỗng, dispatch luôn đỗ. Bất biến phải giữ: work item (nhất là trường proof — được chạy như lệnh shell) do chính người dùng tạo; không bao giờ nạp việc từ nguồn ngoài khi chưa có vòng kiểm (security panel, ghi trong hợp đồng handoff).
- **RUL7 (schema item mang đủ chất liệu trả lời sáu câu hỏi harness).** Lớp lỗi lạ → dừng, không bao giờ mặc định thử-lại (fail-safe).
- **RUL8 (deps phải trỏ id tồn tại, cấm tự trỏ).** Bước gặt-lại làm chạy-lại-sau-crash an toàn tự thân: không việc nào vô hình, không commit đôi, không worktree rò (reliability panel — 3 blocker vá trước khi code).
- **RUL9 (thực thi khi dev).** Mọi kiểm chứng chạy trong Claude Code bằng subscription: suite dùng executor giả (0 token), worker thật qua claude CLI login. API key chỉ hợp lệ khi tính năng đang test là executor-cắm-ngoài, và là key của môi trường người dùng (per 774b73ef).
- **RUL10 (diễn tập không chạm log thật).** Nhật ký sự kiện append-only bất biến → một event diễn tập lọt vào là rác vĩnh viễn: canary/drill LUÔN chạy trên repo mồi dùng-xong-vứt; chỉ dogfood việc-thật mới ghi log thật — và đó là lịch sử vận hành chủ đích (per f3a16887).
- **RUL11 (thang kiểm chứng).** T0 suite executor-giả mọi commit · T1 dogfood việc thật hằng ngày · T1c canary khai-môi-trường (worker tự báo pwd/git-root/doctrine nó thấy, verify assert từng dòng) định kỳ và sau mỗi đổi harness · T2 máy-trắng (HOME giả + credential tối thiểu) trước release (per f3a16887). Bất biến nền: mỗi agent khởi đầu tại project-root CỦA NÓ — thợ ở xưởng, worker ở git-root của worktree nó đứng.
- **RUL12 (khoá liên-tiến-trình).** Mỗi kho chỉ một runner sống tại một thời điểm: đầu MỌI lần chạy (trước cả bước gặt-lại — gặt cũng ghi trạng thái), runner chiếm khoá độc quyền trong vùng trạng thái, ghi định danh tiến trình của mình. Kho đang có runner sống → lần chạy mới thoát «bận» bằng mã thoát riêng (không trùng mã nào hiện hành): không ghi trạng thái, không đụng worktree, không đụng khoá của người giữ. Khoá của runner đã chết (crash để lại, hoặc nội dung không chứng minh được chủ sống) → **dọn-rồi-nhường**: kiểm nội dung sát trước khi xoá (đổi rồi thì không đụng), xoá xong lượt đó vẫn lui ra «bận» — không lượt chạy nào vừa xoá khoá vừa tự chiếm trong cùng một lần, nên hai lượt cùng gặp khoá chết không thể cướp khoá mới của nhau; lượt kế tiếp chiếm khoá sạch (sau crash, phục hồi trọn trong hai lượt). Khoá luôn được nhả trên mọi đường thoát.
- **RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại).** Mỗi lần dispatch, runner ghi bản ghi outcome ở CẢ hai đầu: nửa dự đoán lúc nhận việc, nửa thực tế ở MỌI kết cục cuối — thành đề xuất, bị đỗ, hay bị dừng — không bao giờ chỉ ghi khi thành công. Giá trị thực tế luôn lấy từ phép đo goal-check/kiểm nhánh của chính runner, không bao giờ từ báo cáo tự khai của trợ lý (per phase-3-compound-learning / 1a80b4d3; mở rộng nguyên tắc "không tin lời trợ lý" đã khóa ở RUL3 (thứ tự ghi bất biến: sự kiện vào nhật ký trước, bản chiếu cập nhật sau)). Bản ghi outcome đọc lại được qua lệnh đọc-thuần `fgos check` của tầng Work-State — runner không có verb ghi riêng cho việc này.
- **RUL14 (quét nghiên-cứu chạy trước dispatch, bất kể mode).** Mỗi lượt chạy, ngay sau gặt-lại và trước khi tìm việc thi công, runner GIAO TOÀN BỘ item đang ở stage `discovery` + `status: todo` cho một worker thật, rồi áp đúng phán quyết mà chính worker đó phát ra — không đọc/không rẽ nhánh theo field `mode` của item (per stage-clarify / 9a19eea5, xem RUL17 (quét chia-việc chạy ngay sau quét nghiên-cứu, trước dispatch, bất kể mode)-RUL19 (`return` mirror trung thực contract `awaiting-approval` của runner, không tin lời) (work-state)). Runner KHÔNG BAO GIỜ tự phán thay: worker không để lại commit nào, hoặc output không mang phán quyết đọc được, thì item đứng nguyên tại chỗ chờ lượt sau — không bao giờ bị đẩy tiếp bừa. Never chạm item `awaiting-human`, và cũng không chạm item đã có người/phiên cầm (`doing`) — cùng luật loại-trừ RUL6 (consumer rẽ nhánh theo mã thoát phạm trù, không bao giờ theo thông điệp) (work-state)/RUL15 (role trên mọi ngã-ngũ tự động của runner) (work-state) áp cho cả bước quét này. Stage `exploring` nằm NGOÀI mọi quét của vòng tự hành: nó là pha cần người, để dành cho một phiên sống. Đây là lưới đỡ: phiên submit sống chết giữa chừng không để lại việc kẹt vô hình. `discovery` là tên stage riêng của `coding`, không domain nào khác khai — nên phép khớp trực tiếp ở đây không bao giờ bắt nhầm item của một domain khác (xem spec Work-State "Mô hình domain").
- **RUL15 (role trên mọi ngã-ngũ tự động của runner).** Mọi ngã-ngũ mà runner TỰ ghi trong vòng dispatch (quét nghiên-cứu cho qua, quét chia-việc cho qua, nhận việc, đề xuất, đỗ) mang `role` = `runner`; ngã-ngũ do phiên sống gọi tay context-discovery/phán chia-việc mang `role` = `session`; ngã-ngũ do người gọi qua lệnh CLI mang `role` = `human` — ba giá trị phủ hết mọi đường ngã-ngũ hiện có, không đường nào bị bỏ sót (per phase-3-compound-learning S3-closeout / 96a65365; xem spec Work-State "Bản ghi settlement"). Từ vựng `role` nay có thêm giá trị thứ tư, `system` — cạnh do máy sinh ra như hệ quả của một verb, không do ai quyết định — dùng trên cạnh park nội bộ (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc)); một cạnh park không phải một ngã-ngũ nên không tính vào ba giá trị trên.
- **RUL16 (điểm entropy luôn giải thích được + luôn kèm xu hướng).** Điểm entropy trên `metrics entropy` không bao giờ là một con số đơn độc — luôn kèm các thành phần đã cộng nên nó, và luôn so với snapshot gần nhất (lần đầu là baseline). Seal-digest chỉ im lặng một mệnh đề khi kênh đó thật sự không có gì để nói (số đếm hiện tại VÀ chênh lệch đều bằng 0) — một kênh có dữ liệu nhưng không đổi ...
- **RUL17 (quét chia-việc chạy ngay sau quét nghiên-cứu, trước dispatch, bất kể mode).** Mỗi lượt chạy, ngay sau quét nghiên-cứu và trước khi tìm việc thi công, runner đọc lại view tươi rồi quét TOÀN BỘ item ở stage thỏa bước Chia-việc của domain của chính nó (`planning` cho `coding`) — CỘNG THÊM item còn nằm ở tên stage di sản `decompose`, một alias chỉ-để-rút-cạn không item mới nào còn được tạo ở đó — với `status: todo`, rồi chạy phán chia-việc; không đọc/không rẽ nhánh theo field `mode` của item. Bước quét này KHÔNG gọi model: nó chỉ cho đi thẳng một item mà bản kế hoạch đã ghi tự khai là một-mảnh, mọi trường hợp khác nó không làm gì cả và chờ một phiên sống phán tay — sinh con là hành động ghi thật, không bao giờ được đoán. Never chạm item `awaiting-human` — cùng luật loại-trừ RUL6 (consumer rẽ nhánh theo mã thoát phạm trù, không bao giờ theo thông điệp) (work-state)/RUL15 (role trên mọi ngã-ngũ tự động của runner) (work-state) áp cho bước quét này. Đọc view tươi sau quét nghiên-cứu nghĩa là một item vừa rời `discovery` trong CÙNG lượt chạy vẫn được quét chia-việc ngay, không đợi lượt sau (per stage-decompose / 43f257ae, xem spec Work-State "Giai đoạn Chia-việc").
- **RUL18 (gặt-lại claim-role-aware — không giẫm người/phiên cầm qua cửa pull).** Bước gặt-lại lúc khởi động CHỈ gặt claim mà chính runner đã tạo và crash giữa chừng; một item `doing` mang `claimRole` `human`/`session` (đến từ `fgos take` — spec Work-State "Cửa pull giao–nhận việc") không bao giờ bị reclaim, dù nó không mang commit/proof nào — người/phiên cầm việc vô thời hạn cho tới khi chính họ `fgos return`. Đây là một THU HẸP thuần túy của tập item vốn đã bị reap — không mở rộng, không giảm an toàn của gặt-lại cho claim của chính runner (per stage-decompose, chốt tại validating sau 1 BLOCKER / 43f257ae, 6f2cbc47, a30a3d3c).
- **RUL19 (`return` mirror trung thực contract `awaiting-approval` của runner, không tin lời).** Cửa pull `return` chỉ chuyển `doing → awaiting-approval` sau khi TỰ đo — không tin báo cáo của người gọi — cả ba: working tree host repo sạch, HEAD tiến so `headAtTake` ghi lúc `take`, và verify thật của item chạy xanh qua CÙNG hàm goal-check runner dùng (`runGoalCheck`, `src/runner/goal-check.mjs`) — mở rộng nguyên tắc "không tin lời trợ lý" đã khóa ở RUL3 (thứ tự ghi bất biến: sự kiện vào nhật ký trước, bản chiếu cập nhật sau)/RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại) sang tác nhân cửa pull. Verify đỏ đi đúng đường `blocked` + friction lớp `verification`, y hệt đường đỗ chấm-trượt của chính runner; không sinh settlement ở `return` (settlement thuộc cạnh `→done`, per stage-decompose — xem spec Work-State) (per stage-decompose / 43f257ae, 6f2cbc47, a30a3d3c).
- **RUL60 (`return` mang thêm khuyến nghị frozen-judge — advisory, không bao giờ chặn, per STR63).** Ngay khi `check.passed` (cả hai nhánh nguồn: branch-source qua `branchHeadAtTake→branchHead`, main-source qua `headAtTake→head`), `return` tính `changedFilesSince(cwd, from, to)` (`git diff --name-only`, KHÔNG dùng `changedFiles` của `merge.mjs` — hàm đó cố định trả `[]` cho item không phải nguồn runner, tức luôn rỗng với chính item cửa pull mà `return` phục vụ) rồi chấm qua `frozenJudgeHits(changedFiles, item.footprint)` (`src/runner/frozen-judge.mjs`, domain layer thuần — cổng mẫu `FROZEN_JUDGE_PATTERNS` bê nguyên từ frozen-judge của bee, khớp exact-path với `footprint` đã khai, không hỗ trợ prefix-thư-mục/glob, đúng quy ước `footprintOverlap` sẵn có). Kết quả gắn vào field `frozenJudgeHits` của JSON trả về — KHÔNG BAO GIỜ đổi `passed`/đường đi `blocked`, thuần advisory (per - str63-frozen-judge-fgos, xem forgent workshop `docs/history/str63-frozen-judge-fgos/CONTEXT.md`).
- **RUL20 (cổng duyệt là cửa MỘT DUY NHẤT cho mọi đề xuất, bất kể nguồn).** `review`/`approve`/`reject` hành động trên CẢ hai nguồn đề xuất — runner (nhánh `fgw/<id>`) và pull-door (dải `headAtTake→headAtReturn`) — qua cùng một luật, không hai bộ quy tắc song song; đề xuất di sản (thiếu cả nhánh lẫn cặp head) degrade trung thực (một cảnh báo, không throw) thay vì bị từ chối hoàn toàn (per pr-lifecycle / 1359ab5e).
- **RUL21 (merge sạch → done tự động; gãy → hủy sạch merge dở + blocked có lý do).** `approve` trên nguồn runner không bao giờ để main ở trạng thái merge dở trên bất kỳ đường thoát nào: conflict hoặc verify đỏ sau merge đều `git merge --abort` (main nguyên vẹn byte-for-byte, chứng minh bằng spike + test thật) rồi đậu item ở `blocked` mang lý do cụ thể (`merge-conflict`/`verify-fail-post-merge`) — KHÔNG tự rebase, KHÔNG halt cả vòng runner. `done` qua approve luôn mang role `human` (per pr-lifecycle / 1359ab5e — người chạy approve là ngã-ngũ, merge chỉ là hệ quả cơ học, per vision §8 "người ở cổng").
- **RUL22 (reject không bao giờ đảo lịch sử).** `reject` là một move FSM thuần `awaiting-approval→todo` mang `reason`; không bao giờ gọi một lệnh git nào, kể cả cho một đề xuất pull-door đã có code thật trên main — code đó ở lại như lịch sử, `reject` chỉ từ-chối coi-là-xong, không revert/rewrite (per pr-lifecycle / 1359ab5e).
- **RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker).** Prompt dựng cho worker (`buildPrompt`) mang thêm một mục `# Human feedback` TÙY CHỌN khi item mang câu trả lời làm-rõ mới nhất (fold từ cổng chờ-người, xem spec Work-State "Bản ghi cổng-người") và/hoặc lý do từ-chối/đỗ mới nhất (`item.reason`, xem spec Work-State Data Dictionary #18): câu trả lời in NGUYÊN VĂN dưới nhãn quyết-định-cuối-cùng-ràng-buộc, lý do mới nhất in NGUYÊN VĂN dưới nhãn ưu-tiên-sửa-trước-tiên. Vắng cả hai → mục này KHÔNG xuất hiện, prompt giữ nguyên byte-identical hình cũ (cộng thêm thuần, không phá vỡ hợp đồng 4 section pin sẵn có). Runner đọc lại view TƯƠI ngay trước khi spawn worker (item truyền vào dispatch có thể cũ hơn move gần nhất của chính lượt gặt-lại/quét) rồi truyền `feedback: {answer, reason}` xuống `spawnWorker`. Đây là cách một vòng reject hội tụ: dogfood-thật cho thấy không có mục này, worker vòng sau lặp lại đúng đề xuất vừa bị từ chối vì không thấy lý do (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e).
- **RUL24 (một-người-ghi vẫn giữ nguyên dưới song song, qua một cửa ghi tuần tự).** Dù nhiều việc thi công đồng thời trong một mẻ, MỌI thay đổi trạng thái (nhận việc, đề xuất, đỗ, nhập) đi qua ĐÚNG một cửa ghi tuần tự — một giao dịch ghi trọn vẹn rồi mới tới giao dịch kế tiếp, không bao giờ hai thay đổi chen lẫn nhau giữa chừng. Đây là hệ quả trực tiếp của RUL1 (sự thật duy nhất là nhật ký sự kiện append-only, bản chiếu chỉ là dẫn xuất) dưới điều kiện mới: song song ở việc THỰC THI (nhiều worker chạy đồng thời), không phải ở việc GHI (per fan-out-parallel).
- **RUL25 (cây chính chỉ nhận nguyên một tính năng đã xong, không mảnh dở — SUPERSEDE quyết định trước đó).** Một việc CON không bao giờ nhập thẳng vào cây chính — nó nhập vào nhánh của GỐC nó; chỉ đề xuất của chính GỐC (sau khi mọi con đã xong) mới nhập vào cây chính, đúng một lần cho cả tính năng. Điều này THAY quyết định trước đây ("mỗi việc một đề xuất, thẳng vào cây chính") trong bối cảnh một việc có con — quyết định cũ vẫn đúng nguyên vẹn cho một việc ĐỘC LẬP (không con), đi thẳng đường cũ không đổi (per fan-out-parallel / 2e92b7a5, supersede-in-context quyết định pr-lifecycle).
- **RUL26 (quyền-sở-hữu-gốc — mọi con của một gốc về tay cùng một chủ trong một lượt chạy).** Lúc con ĐẦU TIÊN của một gốc được nhận trong một lượt chạy, gốc đó gắn chủ; con tiếp theo của CÙNG gốc chỉ được nhận bởi ĐÚNG chủ đó — một chủ khác giành nhận bị từ chối (cùng khuôn kỳ-vọng-lệch của mọi cửa nhận việc khác), việc đó ở lại chờ mẻ sau. Chủ xả khi gốc xong. Bảo vệ nguyên tắc "mọi con của một gốc chung một không gian làm việc" (per fan-out-parallel).
- **RUL27 (nhập gốc→cây chính bắt CẢ xung đột văn bản LẪN trôi ngữ nghĩa im lặng).** Một GỐC từng có con, lúc nhập vào cây chính, được kiểm CẢ hai: nhập có xung đột văn bản không, VÀ sau khi nhập (chưa chốt) verify của chính gốc còn xanh không trên cây đã nhập — verify đỏ ở bước này là TRÔI ngữ nghĩa (nhập sạch nhưng kết hợp gãy), bị coi ngang xung đột văn bản: hủy sạch, cây chính không bao giờ giữ một nhập xanh-mà-gãy (per fan-out-parallel / f0c40acc). Vì đây là phép kiểm DUY NHẤT cho cả cây hậu duệ, verify của gốc phải đủ mạnh lúc soạn — verify mỏng bỏ lọt trôi ngữ nghĩa.
- **RUL28 (đồng bộ-lại sạch = cơ học không đếm; làm-lại tay = có đếm).** Một việc đỗ vì gãy nhập được đồng bộ-lại: nếu sau khi kéo đích mới nhất vào, nhập sạch VÀ verify xanh, việc trở lại sẵn sàng nộp lại theo đường cơ học (không qua "đang làm", không tính vào ngân sách chống-lặp của việc) — phân biệt với người CHỌN cầm việc qua cửa pull để tự làm-lại tay, đường đó QUA "đang làm" như bình thường và ĐƯỢC đếm (per fan-out-parallel).
- **RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người CUỐI CÙNG của chính việc, per-item, trigger-set đóng, executing-phase-only scoping).** Cổng chặn dispatch (khác `visitCount` lifetime metric ở RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại) — xem Data Dictionary #4/#4b) đếm `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent`: số lần việc vào `doing` **ở stage executing của chính domain** KỂ TỪ sự kiện người cuối cùng của CHÍNH việc đó. Trước claim-lock (str83-fgos-slash-commands), `take`/`pick` chỉ mở frontier (executing-stage items), nên counting lifetime `todo→doing` moves tương đương counting chỉ dispatch attempts thực. Claim-lock cho phép `pick --id` cầm item ở các stage đầu vòng (`discovery`/`exploring`/`planning`, cộng tên di sản `decompose`) — một claim-release cycle ở đó (pick → phán chia-việc release `doing→todo` → pick lại ở executing) KHÔNG phải attempt dispatch và không được silent-ăn ngân sách của executing-phase attempts thực (per claim-lock §3a/§3c). Số liệu dẫn xuất chỉ từ `to:'doing'` moves mà item đã ở executing stage (mirror frontier.mjs's eligibility check). Trigger-set đóng — chỉ hai hình reset: việc rời `awaiting-human` bằng một câu trả lời của người (`answer`, role `human`), hoặc một move mang `reason` VỚI role `human` (reject/park do người quyết). Một lần resume trần (`blocked→todo` không `reason`), một lần người `take` việc (`blocked→doing`, role `human`, không `answer`/`reason`), và mọi move của chính runner (kể cả park mang `reason` của chính nó) đều KHÔNG reset — chỉ tính là một visit như mọi lần khác. Không có sự kiện người nào của việc → ngân sách bằng đúng lifetime `visitCount` executing-scoped (một vòng lỗi máy thuần vẫn chết ở trần 3, không đổi). `MAX_VISITS=3` và mọi call site của `visitCount` (outcome/metric đã ship) giữ nguyên — chỉ điểm CHẶN DISPATCH đổi công thức đếm (per human-rounds / 5a6900b2, per claim-lock §6 / code-review finding).
- **RUL30 (cửa người-hoàn-tất một đề xuất nguồn-nhánh bị đỗ — mở rộng take/return, không verb mới).** Một việc `blocked` mang nhánh đề xuất còn sống (`fgw/<id>`) — kể cả bị đỗ do chạm trần chống-lặp — có cửa công khai để người hoàn tất: `take` claim qua cạnh `blocked→doing` sẵn có, ghi `branchHeadAtTake` (HEAD của NHÁNH lúc take — discriminator DUY NHẤT của nguồn-nhánh, không dùng `classifySource` để phân biệt vì nó ưu-tiên-nhánh); người commit thêm lên nhánh; `return` kiểm `branchHeadAtTake` TRƯỚC mọi guard main-based (cây làm việc chính của người không bao giờ bị đọc/đụng), verify chạy trong một worktree TẠM, DETACHED tại đúng SHA của nhánh (không bao giờ checkout theo tên, không `reclaimOrphanedCheckout` — an toàn cả khi người đang đứng trên chính nhánh đó ở một worktree khác) → sạch + xanh → `awaiting-approval` mang `branchHeadAtReturn`; **TUYỆT ĐỐI không ghi `headAtReturn`** cho nguồn-nhánh (trộn hai marker cho `reviewDiff` một dải vô nghĩa). Không commit mới trên nhánh, hoặc verify đỏ trong worktree tạm → từ chối rõ lý do, việc giữ nguyên `doing`. Một đề xuất hoàn tất theo đường này đọc nguồn là `runner` như bình thường (nhánh `fgw/<id>` còn sống — không cần đổi `classifySource`/`merge.mjs`) và đi qua CÙNG cổng duyệt PR nội bộ (per human-rounds / 5a6900b2, xem spec Work-State "Cửa pull giao–nhận việc").

unit.text: - **RUL62 (`return --no-new-commits-ok` — đóng sổ việc đã xong THẬT từ trước lúc claim, không phải "tin lời").** Khi `branchAheadCount`/`aheadCount` <= 0 (chưa có commit mới kể từ `branchHeadAtTake`/`headAtTake`) NHƯNG cờ `--no-new-commits-ok` được truyền, `return` bỏ qua đúng MỘT bước — throw "chưa tiến" — rồi tiếp tục y hệt đường thường: verify thật vẫn chạy qua CÙNG `runGoalCheck`, xanh mới `awaiting-approval` (ghi `actual.aheadCount: 0`), đỏ vẫn `blocked` + friction lớp `verification` như thường (cờ không bao giờ tắt verify). Trước khi bỏ qua, một cổng riêng (`assertNoPriorBlockedOutcome`) từ chối cờ nếu `outcomes[id].actual.outcome` từng là `'blocked'` bất kỳ lúc nào trong lịch sử item (toàn item, không chỉ lượt claim hiện tại — `view.outcomes[id].actual` sống sót qua một lượt tái-claim vì tái-claim chỉ ghi `predicted`, không đụng `actual`) — chặn đúng lỗ hổng cờ có thể mở: tái claim một việc đã `blocked` thật, gọi cờ với không commit mới, hy vọng verify xanh vì lý do khác. Cờ chỉ đóng sổ việc CHƯA từng return, không bao giờ cứu một lượt thử lại đã thất bại thật. Mặc định (không cờ) của `return` giữ nguyên byte-for-byte cho mọi caller hiện có (per - return-close-pre-done-work / tsk-4on, xem `docs/history/return-close-pre-done-work/CONTEXT.md`+`plan.md`).
