unit.text:
- **RUL63 (`executors.<id>.allowCrossProvider` — cổng governance chặn nội dung prompt rời hệ Claude qua 1 backend không rõ nguồn, mặc định hạn chế; phạm vi mở rộng thành kind-độc-lập, tsk-in1-4 D5).** `resolveExecutorConfig` (`src/runner/dispatch.mjs`), sau khi giải executor thắng cuộc theo thứ tự ưu tiên `executors.<executorId>` > `executor` (tsk-62v; rung trung gian `executors.<tier>` đã rút, tsk-in1-2), kiểm thêm: nếu `command` CUỐI CÙNG đã giải KHÔNG nằm trong danh sách CLI-Claude đã biết (`CLAUDE_CLI_COMMANDS`, hiện chỉ `'claude'` — cố ý KHÔNG dùng chung `KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES`, vì danh sách đó có `'codex'`, một CLI không phải Claude) VÀ executor không mang `allowCrossProvider: true` tường minh → ném `RunnerConfigError` ngay tại thời điểm resolve, TRƯỚC bất kỳ dispatch nào — không bao giờ âm thầm gửi nội dung ra backend khác. Phép kiểm dựa trên `command` CUỐI CÙNG đã giải (không phải `kind` khai báo đơn thuần, không phải `provider` — nhãn hiển thị tự khai tùy ý, có thể spoof). Miễn trừ DUY NHẤT: một executor giải qua `buildAgentTypeExecutor` (không tự khai `command`/`adapter`/`invocations` — chỉ `agentType`) luôn tái dùng `command` của `executor` toàn cục, trên thực tế luôn là Claude, nên phép kiểm này tự vô hiệu cho đường đó — KHÔNG phải một miễn trừ theo `kind`. Trước tsk-in1-4, phạm vi CHỈ áp dụng cho `kind: "cli"` (`kind: "task"` được miễn trừ thẳng theo khai báo — lỗ hổng thật: 1 executor `kind:"task"` không có `agentType`, rơi thẳng về `executor` toàn cục qua đường KHÁC `buildAgentTypeExecutor`, đáng lẽ vẫn cần kiểm nếu `executor` đó không phải Claude, nhưng được bỏ qua nhầm). tách `kind` khỏi vai trò "cờ miễn trừ" — `agy` (`kind:"agent"`) VẪN cần `allowCrossProvider` cho backend `agy` CLI không phải Claude của nó, y hệt trước. Vắng mặt hoặc `false` ở `allowCrossProvider` luôn nghĩa là CHẶN (mặc định hạn chế) — không bao giờ đọc ngược thành "cho phép trừ khi đánh dấu nhạy cảm" (per - tsk-32n, xem `docs/history/capacity-cross-provider-governance/CONTEXT.md`+`plan.md`).
- **RUL65 (`executors.<id>.kind` là `agent`/`tool` — trục BẢN CHẤT, tách khỏi `invocations[].via` — trục CƠ CHẾ GỌI; tsk-in1-4 D5/D8/D9).** Trước item này, `kind` gánh 2 vai đồng thời: mượn thẳng `tool-registry.mjs`'s `KINDS` (`cli`/`binary`/`mcp`/`skill`) làm cơ chế probe-presence CHO CẢ dispatch, cộng thêm `'task'` cho dispatch native — 1 field, 2 câu hỏi khác nhau ("đây LÀ gì" và "gọi NÓ bằng cách nào"), khiến `gitnexus`'s `kind:"mcp"` và `herdr`'s `kind:"cli"` phải mang nghĩa kép không liên quan. Từ tsk-in1-4: `EXECUTOR_KINDS = ['agent', 'tool']` — `agent` = 1 persona sống, có thể dispatch-native khi phiên gọi có live Task access (`decideExecutorDispatchMechanism` đọc `kind === 'agent'`, không còn `'task'`); `tool` = cơ học, presence-only theo thiết kế gốc (`gitnexus`/`herdr`), dù về mặt cơ chế 1 entry `kind:"tool"` khai `command`/`args` phẳng vẫn dispatch được qua `resolveExecutorConfig` bình thường — `kind` chỉ quyết định tính đủ-điều-kiện-native, không phải có-dispatch-được-hay-không. Cơ chế gọi dời hẳn sang `invocations[].via` — `INVOCATION_VIA = ['cli', 'task', 'mcp']` (`'binary'`/`'skill'`/`'http'` bỏ khi gộp từ vocab cũ của `tool-registry.mjs`, `'api'` chưa quay lại — 0 producer lịch sử, bằng chứng qua `.fgos/events.jsonl`). `tool-registry.mjs`'s `toolsFromExecutors` (`src/state/tool-registry.mjs`) đọc probe-kind/probe-command từ `invocations[0].via`/`.command`, không còn từ `executor.kind` nữa — hệ quả trực tiếp của việc tách trục.

Quota/rate-limit quarantine account; auth/login/token quarantine dạng manual-clear; credential provisioning/config/test/confinement/work-product failure không quarantine. Chủ máy đặt quarantine tay bằng `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity quarantine --provider <provider> --account <id> --until <ISO tương lai> --reason "<why>"` (quota-limit tạm thời, `detail.kind: owner`; unknown account hoặc `--until` không ở tương lai bị refuse; ghi vào state thật của máy, không theo `--dir`). Classifier cũng đọc giờ reset tuyệt đối codex in ("try again at 6:02 PM", giờ local, lần kế tiếp). Manual clear duy nhất là `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine --provider <provider> --account <id> --reason "<why>"` (unknown provider/account bị refuse; non-quarantined account bị refuse trừ khi `--force`). `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` và `fgos doctor` chỉ report; doctor không auto-clear auth quarantine. `readOnlyExecutorRedirects` vẫn giữ nguyên trong slice này; không có `providerFallback`, `providerRuntimes`, `providers.<provider>.models`, six-tier runtime wiring, cross-provider fallback, hay retry loop trong rotator.

unit.title: Unheaded block 72
unit.sample: Provider failure inside a Unit run goes to another account before another provider (decision 0058). A round that ends `provider-limit` is retried as the same executor and invocatio
unit.text: Provider failure inside a Unit run goes to another account before another provider (decision 0058). A round that ends `provider-limit` is retried as the same executor and invocation under a fresh `-fb<n>` assignment id while another account of that executor's provider is usable (listed in the inventory, not quarantined) and fewer retries than that provider has accounts were spent on this candidate; the lease then ranks the next account as it always does. Only when no account is left does `nextCandidate` walk the capability pool, skipping provider families whose login failed in this unit and still preferring a family the sibling seats did not use. A process that exits non-zero with a dead-credential wording (`AUTH_FAILURE_PATTERNS`, e.g. pi "No API key found for openrouter.") in its last five stderr lines settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: credential`, so the account is quarantined as `auth-token`. A process that exits the same way with a used-up quota as its last words (`QUOTA_LIMIT_PATTERNS` in `provider-auth-failure.mjs`, line-start anchored after an optional `ERROR:`; measured: codex "ERROR: You’ve hit your usage limit. ... try again at 11:39 PM.", 2026-10-13) settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: quota`, with or without an account lease, so a headless cli-spawn round rotates and walks like a pane round; a leased account is quarantined `quota-limit` until the reset the provider printed (the existing `until`, no separate retry field), and a quota stop does not exclude the provider family. The capacity classifier reads the same wordings from the stderr tail only. Rescheduling a run whose accounts and candidates are all used up is not done here (Workflow runner, separate decision). Each attempt records `fallbackFrom.kind` (`account-rotation` or `next-candidate`).

  - **Gate B1 (shape-theo-via, `validateInvocationShape`).** Không ép hình dạng executor (`command` string + `args` array) lên MỌI invocation bất kể `via` — `via:"cli"` cần đủ hình dạng executor thật (sẽ spawn thật); `via:"mcp"` chỉ cần `command` là 1 định danh không rỗng (không bao giờ spawn, không cần `args`); `via:"task"` không cần cả hai (dispatch native không mang subprocess argv).
  - **Gate B2 (chọn đúng invocation theo `via`, `resolveExecutorConfig`).** Không lấy `invocations[0]` mù — chọn ĐÚNG entry có `via:"cli"` (cơ chế DUY NHẤT `resolveExecutorConfig` thật sự dispatch), bất kể thứ tự khai trong mảng.
 - **Gate B3 (throw tường minh khi không dispatch-được, `resolveExecutorConfig`).** Khi 1 executor khai `invocations` nhưng KHÔNG entry nào `via:"cli"` (như `gitnexus`) — ném `RunnerConfigError` ngay, không bao giờ âm thầm rơi về `executor` toàn cục như thể executor đó chỉ mang metadata (khác hẳn 1 executor thật sự không khai `invocations`/`command`/`adapter`/`agentType` nào — ca đó vẫn rơi về `executor` toàn cục bình thường).

unit.text: - **RUL66 (`EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS`' chữ ký tổng quát hoá thành `(invocation, opts)`; `'api'` quay lại `INVOCATION_VIA` với 1 adapter `http` thật; tsk-in1-5).** Trước item này `EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS` map tên adapter → hàm `(command, args, cwd, opts)` — 1 hình dạng định hình sẵn theo CLI argv, đúng "bẫy B1" (tsk-in1-4's gate B1 đã đóng cho `validateInvocationShape`, nhưng port thực thi bên dưới vẫn ép mọi adapter vào khuôn CLI). unit.title: Unheaded block 78
unit.sample: - **RUL67 (dispatch chokepoint hiện rõ trên màn hình — `spawnWorker`, cả 2 nhánh `executeExecutorCli`).** Trước item này, dispatch xảy ra hoàn toàn im lặng trên stdout/stderr — kết
unit.text:
- **RUL67 (dispatch chokepoint hiện rõ trên màn hình — `spawnWorker`, cả 2 nhánh `executeExecutorCli`).** Trước item này, dispatch xảy ra hoàn toàn im lặng trên stdout/stderr — kết quả (`{status, stdout, ...}` hay `{mechanism, ...}`) chỉ trả về giá trị JS/CLI JSON, không có tín hiệu nào cho người đang xem terminal biết "cái gì vừa được gọi, ai trả lời, qua đường nào" trước khi nó xảy ra. Mỗi chokepoint dispatch thật (nơi 1 executor thật sự được thực thi hoặc quyết định hand-back native, không phải nơi chỉ resolve/quyết định suông) giờ in đúng 1 dòng `stderr` ngay trước khi dispatch xảy ra: `fgos: dispatch capability=<...> executor=<...> via=<...> provider=<...> model=<...> tier=<...>`.
 - `spawnWorker` (runner tự dispatch 1 work item): `capability` in ra là kết quả `executorIdForWork` (tên skill executing-stage theo domain/stage — TRỤC KHÁC hẳn danh mục `runner.capabilities`) vì đường này không đi qua `for`/`capabilities` catalog; nhãn dùng `job=` thay vì `capability=` ngay trong dòng in để tránh lẫn 2 khái niệm. `executor` in `(global executor)` khi `cfg.executors` không có entry khớp `executorIdForWork`'s kết quả ('s "miss cố ý").
  - `executeExecutorCli` nhánh in-process (`mechanism:"in-process"`, hand-back cho caller, KHÔNG tự spawn): dòng in thêm `agentType=<...>`, `provider`/`model`/`tier` đều `n/a` (chưa resolve tới bước đó).
  - `executeExecutorCli` nhánh out-of-process (tự spawn thật): dòng in đầy đủ `provider`/`model`/`tier` như thật sẽ dùng để spawn — in NGAY TRƯỚC lệnh `adapterFn(...)` thật, không phải sau.
  - `capability` (2 nhánh `executeExecutorCli`) ưu tiên `purpose` (flag `--for` caller truyền vào) khi có; không thì đọc `cfg.executors.<id>.for` của chính executor đó (nhiều giá trị nối bằng dấu phẩy) làm nhãn thông tin; rỗng thì in `(none declared)`.
  - Thuần diagnostic (`process.stderr.write`) — không phải phần giá trị trả về của bất kỳ hàm nào, không ai đọc lại nó; không đổi hành vi/return-value hiện có của `spawnWorker`/`executeExecutorCli`.

unit.text: Fallback (Provider Capacity, tầng 1) từng chọn invocation MẶC ĐỊNH của candidate fallback một cách mù — khi 1 executor mang nhiều invocation khác `confinement` (executor-id-consolidation), phép chọn mù đó có thể lặng lẽ hạ cấp 1 primary có confinement xuống 1 fallback KHÔNG confinement. `selectConfinedInvocationId` (`resolve.mjs`) đóng gap này: kiểm CẤU TRÚC thuần ("candidate có invocation nào khai confinement không"), không bao giờ kiểm ngữ nghĩa policy (việc đó vẫn thuộc Confinement Authority, `confinement/authority.mjs`, không đụng tới) — primary có confinement mà fallback không tìm được invocation nào có confinement thì bị refuse thẳng, không âm thầm dispatch hở. - **RUL72 (Gom thang tier/rigor: 2 thang + 1 bảng, xoá mọi lớp chồng; tier-rigor-vocabulary-consolidation, 2026-09-30).**
  Thay thế RUL69 (vocab modelTier 6 mức thay 5 mức cũ) về cơ chế map model và chuẩn hoá từ vựng toàn repo:
  1. Bên cầu (việc cần gì): từ duy nhất là `rigor = low | standard | high | critical` (thay thế `minTier`, `minRigor`, `mode`). `rigor` gộp chỉ-nâng qua các scope (Workflow/Unit → Operation → Actor → Assignment → CLI), rồi gộp sàn theo loại việc `capabilities.<cap>.rigor`.
  2. Bên cung (khẩu vị owner): ánh xạ qua đúng một bảng config bắt buộc `runner.rigorToTier[rigor] → tier` (`nano|mini|standard|advanced|flagship|frontier`), sau đó chọn model tại `runner.modelPolicies[provider][tier]`.
  3. Override tường minh: `--tier` / `actors[].tier` là kênh placement tường minh (chỉ-nâng, có provenance `tierSource`); definition/operation dùng `tier` bị từ chối.
  4. Work: tách `work.tier` thành `work.size` (độ lớn, không bao giờ tới model) và `work.rigor` (tuỳ chọn, discovery phán). Item cũ có `risk: heavy` và chưa có `rigor` được đọc thành `rigor: high` ở đường đọc duy nhất.
  5. Sàn theo loại việc `capabilities.<cap>.rigor` là sàn duy nhất theo loại việc, có hiệu lực ở cả đường coordination lẫn Work. Khối `capabilities.*.overrides` bị xoá hoàn toàn.
  6. Xoá vĩnh viễn không lặp lại: `minTier`, `minRigor`, `QUALITY_TIER_BRIDGE`, `QUALITY_MODE_VALUES`, `DEFAULT_TIER_TO_POLICY`, `rigorOverrides`, `runner.models`, `capabilities.*.overrides`. Test guard tự động chặn chúng quay lại.

- **RUL73 (dispatch KHÔNG biết Work, domain hay bước — tầng Work tra rồi truyền vào; Work không còn `stage`).** `src/runner/dispatch/**` và `src/runner/execution/**` không import `src/state/**`, `src/workflow/**` hay bất kỳ module tầng Work (`work-compat`, `work-dispatch`, `operation-choice`, `loop`, `claim-port`, `prompt-templates`, `intake/`, `verbs/`), và không chứa literal tên domain/bước (guard `test/architecture.test.mjs`, tên đọc từ `domains/*/` trên đĩa). Cụ thể:
  1. Operation/taskSpec/skill của một bước đến từ định nghĩa Workflow (`domains/<d>/workflows/*.yaml`, `steps[].operations`/`skill`), tầng Work đọc qua `src/state/domain-registry.mjs` rồi đưa vào `buildAssignment({ domain, stage, operation, operations })`. Dispatch kiểm `operation ∈ operations` (lỗi `unknown operation ... for stage ...`), ghi danh sách hợp lệ vào `provenance.declared.legalOperations`; `executeAssignment` từ chối một Assignment declared không mang danh sách đó hoặc có `operation` ngoài danh sách (và `dispatch: human-only`). Trường `stage` trên Assignment hiện chỉ còn là nhãn mờ của bước (đổi tên theo đợt thuật ngữ).
  2. [Phần đầu vào còn lại ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only) — `work`/`workItem`/`workExecutorId` thôi là đầu vào của dispatch; `decide --work` nhận hint; `workDispatchContext` không còn trả `work`] Mọi thứ Work-aware chuyển ra tầng Work: `src/runner/operation-choice.mjs` (chọn operation cho bước hiện tại, trước ở `dispatch/`), `src/runner/work-dispatch.mjs` (`spawnWorker`, `resolveAgentTypeForWork`, `resolveWorkForDispatch`, `workDispatchContext`), `src/runner/work-compat.mjs` (`executorIdForWork`, `buildPrompt`, `workCapabilityHints`). Dispatch nhận đầu vào đã phân giải: `workExecutorId` (plan), `capabilityHints`/`agentType` (`executeExecutorCli`/`executeAssignment`), và hook `resolveWork` cho `decide --work` — `dispatch/cli.mjs` không còn bộ đọc event Work riêng, không còn bản chép đồ thị stage.
  3. Work mang `workflowStep` (id bước trong Workflow của domain); `src/state/workflow-stage-graphs.mjs`, `src/state/stage-fsm.mjs` đã xoá — `domain-registry.mjs` (phần vòng đời Work của domain + tra Workflow) và `step-fsm.mjs` (cạnh chuyển bước = `transitions` của Workflow) thay thế. Chi tiết dữ liệu cũ: spec Work-State, "Work không còn `stage`".
  4. Cổng mutating của một unit-run: Assignment mutating phải mang `binding` do `bind()` sinh ra, khớp bản `bind()` tính lại từ `unit.json`, và không được ghim executor khác (`policy.preferExecutor`) — thiếu/khác → từ chối trước khi spawn.

unit.title: Unheaded block 91
unit.sample: - **RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds).** An account quarantined as `auth-token` has no end time: the ow
unit.text: - **RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds).** An account quarantined as `auth-token` has no end time: the owner logs in again by hand and fgOS cannot see it. Instead of waiting for a person to run the clear command, a dispatch that finds **no usable account of the provider** makes one real, cheap call per such account (Codex: `codex exec`; an omp profile, a `home-files` source that lists `agent.db`: `omp -p`; a pi account directory, one that lists `auth.json`: `pi -p`; omp is tested before pi), against the account's own home, not a copy, because the owner uses that home and a renewal belongs there. A call that answers clears the lock (audited as `fgos provider-capacity probe`) and the dispatch goes on; one that does not keeps the lock and records the attempt, and no new call is made for that account within a 30 minute cooldown, however many dispatches ask. Only `auth-token` locks are probed: a quota limit ends by itself and any other manual lock is a person's decision. The call is never made while another account of the provider is usable, runs outside the state lock but inside the account lock of RUL75 (so a renewal made by fgOS cannot overlap it; an account whose lock stays busy past two minutes counts as a failed attempt), stops at the first account that answers, and a failure to probe never blocks the dispatch. A credential layout fgOS cannot name (the agy homes of Gemini) has no call, so that account stays locked for a person. The probe is passed to the dispatch by its callers; a caller that passes none changes nothing.

unit.sample: - **RUL76 (`execute <executorId> --for <capability>`: the caller states the posture; [ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL77 (posture thuộc capability; agent executor không khai `for`) — chốt "execu
unit.text: - **RUL76 (`execute <executorId> --for <capability>`: the caller states the posture; [ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL77 (posture thuộc capability; agent executor không khai `for`) — chốt "executor phải khai capability" đã bỏ]; partly reverses the `execute --for` retirement of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch; `execute --for` đã rút), 2026-10-13).** `execute <id>` with no purpose infers the capability from the executor's own `for` list, a required-confinement capability first (`resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints`). RUL70 (executor id theo `providerModel`; gộp `pi`+`codex` thành `openai`) merged `codex` (`for: [code:review, code:debug]`, both `host-write-denied`) and `pi` (no `for`, the writing invocations) into `openai`, so every `execute openai` became write-denied, whatever the work: a documentation task died with `Read-only file system` when Codex tried to refresh its login under bwrap. That rule itself says executors whose `for` differ should not be merged into one entry; the merge kept the codex `for` without noticing pi had none. Instead of splitting the executor, the two-phase `decide`-then-`execute` pattern now carries the purpose to phase two: `execute <id> --for <capability>` runs under that capability's posture. It is accepted only when the executor declares the capability in `for` or the capability's `prefer` names the executor (otherwise `capability-not-served`, before spawning), so config still says which postures an executor accepts; without `--for` the strictest-first inference stays the fail-closed default. `execute --for` with no executor, or combined with `--assignment`/`--contract`, is still refused. `openai.for` gains `execute`, so writing work goes `execute openai --for execute`, which takes the first `cli` invocation (`codex-cli-bypass-fgovn`, unconfined). `--timeout-ms`/`--idle-timeout-ms` override `runner.timeoutMs`/`runner.idleTimeoutMs` per call. Config for a dispatch whose `--cwd` is a worktree with its own `.fgos/config.json` is read from that worktree (5a42bc376, intended), so a branch behind main also resolves older model tiers.

unit.text:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `/account-locks///`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp--`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env. - **RUL82 (`RunResult.confinement` names the backend that ran, 2026-10-14).** The field was always `null`: settlement compared the requested mode with `'confined'`, a mode that does not exist (`CONFINEMENT_MODES` is `required`/`preferred`/`unconfined`), and the Assignment's confinement requirement never reached settlement. It now comes from `ranConfinementBackend` (`settlement.mjs`): the prepared-invocation record the Confinement Authority published for the launch (`protected/prepared-invocation/.json`, backend type, `none` → `null`), else the attestation the dispatch returned with outcome `enforced`. A requested posture is never evidence of what ran. The field is backend provenance only and attributes no write to the run. - **RUL83 (a snapshot names what changed, never who: correlated write evidence is a warning, 2026-10-14).** Four paths refused a round on a before/after snapshot alone: the CLI/Work doors' `strayWriteError` (repo root dirty paths outside the workspace, 819a61e55), settlement's `read-only-mutation` (`computeChangedFiles` includes every file of every commit that moved the cwd's HEAD during the run), the normalizer's fallback `mutated-dirty-before-files`/`read-only-mutation`, and the read-back evidence floor (`deriveEvidenceFloor`). All four were measured refusing work another session caused: a Doer round (2026-10-14 09:30-10:01) for three reports written into main; two critique reviewers of one panel for files the caller and other lanes wrote; a read-only framing seat (`wf-run-1791954133905-844903ed`) for five reports another session committed to main at 12:03:38. Settlement now decides through one policy, `evaluateAttributionPolicy` (`evidence-attribution.mjs`, previously without a production caller): post-run changes and changed pre-existing dirt are `correlated`, reported in `RunResult.warnings` (`read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`, `outside-write-scope-correlated`: code, level, basis, paths), and the run is accepted; only `proven` writes (a run-bound written-path observer's attestation within its coverage) are refused (`read-only-mutation`, `outside-write-scope`). No such observer exists yet; building one is its own decision. The CLI/Work doors put `stray-write-correlated` (with `repoRoot` and paths) on the dispatch result's `warnings` and print it on stderr. Accepted residual risk: a worker that really writes into the main checkout, the agy incident, is now flagged rather than refused. `rollbackReadOnlyMutations` (a `git reset --soft` plus deletion in the run's cwd, never called) is removed: run against a shared checkout it would undo another session's commit. Decided by the one-door council (`plans/261014-1033-dispatch-operator-improvements/reports/council-261014-1231-dispatch-one-door-conclusion.md`, step 2, finding RT2-3). Work, the consumer, still does not advance on such a result: a read-only result carrying `read-only-mutation-correlated` or `mutated-dirty-before-correlated` (or, read back from disk, a non-empty `evidence.changedFiles`/`mutatedDirtyBeforeFiles`, since stored warnings are as writable as any other field) stops with its own reason `assignment--correlated-mutation` (at planning: `validation-correlated-mutation-do-not-advance-work`), never folded into no-evidence; a round that failed on its own terms (non-zero exit, a timeout settles as 124; a policy refusal, a proven write among them; a provider, resource or contract failure) keeps `assignment--failed`. A stored result read back without its assignment takes its mutation from its operation and recorded `role`, never from a field of its own. The executor CLI door's `stray-write-correlated` (the main checkout changed while an isolated round ran) is kept in `result.json` beside settlement's own warnings but does not stop Work: it cannot have changed the round's own checkout, and on a busy main checkout nearly every round would carry it. Dispatch keeps the warning and does not refuse the round (`src/runner/operation-choice.mjs` `hasReadOnlyCorrelatedMutation`; Lead decision B in `plans/261014-1400-two-doors-one-rununit/phase-00-land-finished-lanes.md`). - **RUL84 (one write-scope matcher: a Unit's `writes` has one spelling, and every "is this path in scope" question goes through `matchesWriteScope`, 2026-10-14; decision 0060).** `writes` entries are normalized once (`./`, `//`, a trailing `/` and `/.` collapse; duplicates dropped, first-seen order kept) and refused when they are `.`, empty, absolute, hold a `..` segment, a `\` or NUL, start with `:` (git pathspec magic) or glue `**` to other characters. Only `*` (inside one segment) and `**` (a whole segment, zero or more segments) are globs; every other character, `[ ] { } ! ?` included, is literal. A plain entry covers the path and everything beneath it; a glob entry must match the whole path; nothing under `.fgos/` is ever in scope, not even for `**`. One leaf module, `src/runner/dispatch/write-scope.mjs` (`canonicalizeWrites`, `expandGenerated`, `matchesWriteScope`, `partitionPaths`), answers for the runner commit, settlement coverage and the Workflow out-of-scope check; git never interprets a scope. Workflow definitions use the same normalizer, and a `writes` that is not an array (YAML `writes:` left empty is `null`) is refused instead of read as `[]`. Config key `runner.generatedPaths: [{ from, also }]` (default `[]`, doctor `runner-generated-paths`): a Unit whose `writes` overlaps a generated source (`from`, e.g. `core/skills/**`) also gets that source's render trees (`also`). The widened scope is stored once in `unit.json#writeScope` when the unit run is created, never recomputed on resume, and is the `writes` of every assignment of that Unit. - **RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope, and refuses to start a writing Unit over a foreign staged index, 2026-10-14; decision 0060, replaces items 1-2 of 0052).** After a passing round the runner stages and commits only the changed paths inside `writeScope`; a path outside it is never committed, and one the agent changed is reported in `commit.outOfScope`. A file already dirty in scope at launch is recorded on the attempt as `preExistingInScope` and never committed by the runner (bounded promise: a file dirty before the round and edited again is not reported). Before a mutating producer is spawned, a non-empty index refuses the round as `policy-refusal` / `foreign-staged-index`, with no pane or worker started. The commit step checks the index again: the staged set must equal the in-scope set (`staged-set-mismatch`) and the committed set must equal that set (`committed-set-mismatch`; the commit stays on the branch); a failure after staging takes back exactly what the runner staged. Before any seat runs, the runner merges it with the trusted git of RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope) — `merge --no-commit --no-ff`, rerere and autostash off — in `src/runner/execution/commit-unit-work.mjs` (`startSyncMerge`, `finishSyncMerge`, `syncMergeState`), orchestrated by `src/runner/execution/unit-sync.mjs`: already in the branch is `up-to-date`; a clean merge is committed by the runner as `chore(sync): merge ` (status `merged`; a commit that is not the merge of `sha` over `head` holding exactly what the merge staged — a hook added a file — fails `committed-set-mismatch` as `execution-failure`, stays on the branch, and the resume is refused until a person takes it off) and the Unit goes on to its pattern, or passes at once when sync-only; a sync never brings the base side of `.fgos/` in: every `.fgos/**` path the merge staged or left conflicted, clean or not, is put back to the branch side (HEAD), a path the base deleted is kept and a path only the base has is not taken — ADR0020 (a worker branch never commits `.fgos/`), the side `fgos-write-rejected` at approve resolves to the target for a `.fgos/` path the branch left unchanged, on every branch, not only `fgw/*`; any other conflict leaves the merge open (status `conflicted`), puts the conflicted paths the scope does not already cover in scope only while the merge is open (`sync.scopeAdded`, read by the effective scope only while `sync.status === 'conflicted'`; `writeScope` itself stays as declared, so a later round cannot write them), and appends a `## Merge to finish` section to the writing seat's brief naming them and telling it never to run git. A refused start leaves no merge open and ends the run: `merge-in-progress` (a merge someone else opened), `foreign-staged-index`, `merge-refused` (git would not start, e.g. a dirty file it would overwrite), `hook-refused` (the pre-commit hook of the main checkout's hooks path refused the clean merge commit; told apart from a git failure by running that hook once more as git runs it, and its words are the detail), `unscopable-conflict-path` (a conflicted path the scope normalizer of RUL84 (one write-scope matcher) would read differently — `*`, a leading `:`, `\`, surrounding whitespace — or holding a control character, since it is also printed into the brief; the merge is aborted) as `policy-refusal`, and `git-error` as `execution-failure`. While the merge is open, the preflight of a writing seat counts only the open MERGE_HEAD equal to `sync.sha` over `sync.head` as the run's own: its conflicted and merge-staged paths are neither a foreign index nor `preExistingInScope`; any other open merge refuses a writing seat (`merge-in-progress`) and `commitUnitWork` never commits over one. After a passing round the runner concludes the merge before the round's own commit: a conflicted file that still holds a line opening with seven or more `<`, `|` or `>` (a larger `conflict-marker-size` included; a file holding a NUL byte is read as binary and not checked) fails the commit `conflict-markers` with `paths`, stages nothing and keeps the merge, so `fgos run --resume` only commits once a person removed them (RUL86 (`fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits)); otherwise it stages the conflicted paths, refuses an index holding anything the merge did not stage (`staged-set-mismatch`, taking back what it staged itself, e.g. a conflicted file the worker turned into a directory), commits with MERGE_HEAD as second parent (a refusing pre-commit hook fails it `hook-refused` with the hook's words and keeps the merge; each `fgos run --resume` tries the commit once, never in a loop), checks parents and committed set (`committed-set-mismatch`), and then commits the rest of the round inside the scope as usual. The round's `commit` carries the merge's own record under `sync`; `runUnit` returns `sync` beside `outcome`; a sync-only unit that needed no worker returns one result `{ role: 'sync', round: 0, commit }` (no `verify`, as for `solo`). A round that did not pass keeps the merge open; a resume checks it first: still open, it runs the seat again over it; concluded by hand (its sha in the branch), it is `merged`; aborted, or HEAD moved, the resume is refused and names the merge. A run that died between starting git and recording the result adopts its own open merge on resume; a first start never adopts one. A resumed sync-only run that was `up-to-date` or `merged` passes again without a worker. Settlement: the writing seat over an open merge carries `assignment.syncConflicts`; those files, dirty at launch, changed during the turn and inside its scope, count as its evidence (`evidence.editedSyncConflicts`), so a seat that only resolves conflicts is not scored `verdict-inconclusive`. Any other file dirty at launch that a seat rewrites still is no evidence, with or without a sync. A units file (`fgos workflow start --units`) naming `syncBase` is refused: a workflow unit's worktree starts from its dependency's branch, and a sync there is not built. Not done: an inline producer over an open merge (inline rounds have no runner commit), a modify/delete conflict whose worker deletes the file is concluded as a deletion. - **RUL98 (`fgos workflow start` kế thừa và phân bổ `--timeout ` và `--account ` cho từng Unit, 2026-10-15).** Workflow run hỗ trợ cờ `--timeout ` (chuỗi thời lượng hợp lệ `1m`..`4h`, phân tích ra `timeoutMs`) và `--account ` (ghim tài khoản nhà cung cấp) giống cơ chế của `--effort`. Cả hai giá trị được lưu bền vững trong payload của sự kiện `workflow.start` và được tái tạo khi `resume`. Về thứ tự ưu tiên timeout: cờ `--timeout` của `fgos run` THẮNG `unit.timeoutMs` của Unit (RUL96 (one run may take its own timeout, from 1m to 4h): override thắng unit), trong khi `--timeout` của `fgos workflow start` NHƯỜNG cho `unit.timeoutMs` tự khai của Unit. Về account: `--account` của workflow chỉ ghim cho các seat thuộc provider sở hữu account đó; các Unit không có seat nào khớp sẽ chạy bình thường không ghim và không làm hỏng workflow; `--account` không tồn tại trong bất kỳ `runner.providers.*.accounts` nào sẽ bị từ chối ngay lúc start trước khi tạo run. - **RUL99 (Bảng mã thoát riêng biệt cho kết cục thực thi của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground`, 2026-10-15).** Các outcome kết thúc không phải `pass` của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground` chuyển sang sử dụng bảng exit code xác định: `pass` = 0, `policy-refusal` = 4 (validation), `provider-limit` = 10, `execution-failure` = 11, `partial-writes` = 12, `blocked` = 13, `findings` = 14. Các lệnh chỉ-đọc như `fgos workflow status` luôn trả về mã thoát 0 bất kể outcome của workflow run. Lệnh `fgos workflow start` ở chế độ detached vẫn trả về mã 0 khi tiến trình daemon được khởi chạy thành công. Định dạng envelope JSON stdout `fgos.v1` giữ nguyên vẹn 100%. - **RUL100 (Doctor check `executor-posture-coverage` chẩn đoán posture readiness của các executor, 2026-10-15).** Check doctor `executor-posture-coverage` kiểm tra tĩnh khả năng áp dụng posture cho các core capabilities (`execute`, `code:implement`) và mọi capability khai báo pool agent (`prefer`). Quá trình kiểm tra chạy hoàn toàn khô qua `bind()`, không spawn tiến trình, không tạo pane herdr, không kích hoạt sandbox. Khi một capability có executor thiếu sandbox bwrap, check báo lỗi `posture-unavailable` (`passed: false`). Khi một capability thiếu pool (`headless-no-executor` / `no-candidate`), check chỉ phát cảnh báo (`passed: true`, tiền tố `warning:`) hướng dẫn khai báo `runner.capabilities..prefer`.

rows.residualText:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `/account-locks///`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places.
